capability: Every Open3D capability record says where it came from, in one shape a tool can read and a guard can check

what_this_closes.row: The fifth row left open when PR 602 merged, raised again by a review lane during PR 982.
what_this_closes.as_found: A review lane found provenance recorded five different ways across these records. Measured against main it is six: a bare top-level `source_commit` in four records, a `provenance` object with `base_commit`/`candidate_commit` in one, a `provenance` object of per-capture notes in another, a `provenance_boundary` statement in a third, a `producing_source` file list in a fourth, and nothing at all in two. An auditor had to learn each file.
what_this_closes.why_i_declined_to_stack_it_on_982: It touches ten records and changes nothing about the frames, the gate or the binding. PROGRAM.md says not to stack unrelated changes onto the first PR.

the_shape.required: A `provenance` object with `source_commit` (a full 40-character hex commit sha, or null with `why_no_source_commit`) and `commit_is_an_ancestor_of_main`.
the_shape.why_the_ancestry_flag: Nine of the ten records name a commit that is not an ancestor of main, and they are right to. The problem was never the values -- it was that a reader could not distinguish a deliberate non-ancestor from a stale or mistyped reference. Stating it turns an ambiguity into a fact.
the_shape.why_i_did_not_do_what_was_asked: The ask was to bind each record to a commit that is an ancestor of the head. That would have meant rewriting nine values to commits the measurements were not taken at, which is falsification, not provenance.

the_finding_this_turned_up.what: At the recorded audit time, nine of ten records that name a provenance commit named one contained by no ref advertised by origin. Those nine records name seven distinct commits. This is a ref-containment result, not proof that GitHub cannot serve an unreferenced object by SHA or that the object exists only in one clone.
the_finding_this_turned_up.why_it_matters_more_than_the_key_names: A uniform key naming an unresolvable commit is tidier and no more auditable. This was not in the original finding and I would not have seen it by standardising key names alone.
the_finding_this_turned_up.what_each_record_now_also_names: The commit on main where that work landed, so a reader has something they can resolve.
the_finding_this_turned_up.how_that_claim_was_checked_rather_than_a: For each stranded commit, a symbol or source line it introduced under npa/ was searched at origin/main and traced with `git log -S`. All seven distinct commits resolve to the same merge.
the_finding_this_turned_up.what_the_probes_do_not_show: That the trees are identical. A probe proves this commit's contribution reached main at that merge, which is strictly weaker and is what the records now say.

a_counting_error_in_my_own_summary_of_th.what_i_wrote: Nine of the ten named commits are on ZERO remote refs. They exist only in the clones that made them, so no other reader  ...
a_counting_error_in_my_own_summary_of_th.what_is_true: Nine RECORDS, seven distinct COMMITS, out of ten commits named. I wrote 'nine of the ten named commits', which conflates the two: three records share 256c26bc9150. The three named commits that are NOT stranded (15b0b11f0bc1, d06e95846286, d22893238d75) are all resolvable, on 328, 18 and 613 origin refs.
a_counting_error_in_my_own_summary_of_th.why_it_slipped: Nine is the number the guard prints, because the guard iterates records. I copied the count into prose about commits without re-deriving it. Every per-record claim was correct; only the roll-up was wrong.

how_the_zero_remote_refs_claim_was_actua.the_problem_with_how_i_first_checked_it: I asserted zero advertised refs from a clone whose only fetch refspec is refs/heads/*, against a remote that advertised 1274 refs of which 933 were PR heads. I consulted roughly a quarter of the advertised refs, and the clone was shallow as well. The ref-containment result was later established; direct object fetchability remains a separate question.
how_the_zero_remote_refs_claim_was_actua.what_the_test_does_now: harness/audit_commit_reachability.py takes git ls-remote as the denominator, fetches every refs/pull/*/head and refs/tags/* into its own namespace, and asks reachability against all of them.
how_the_zero_remote_refs_claim_was_actua.coverage: 1274 advertised refs: 933 PR heads, 11 tags, the rest branches. 23 refs/pull/N/merge refs are skipped because a merge ref has the PR head as an ancestor and cannot contain a commit the head lacks.
how_the_zero_remote_refs_claim_was_actua.how_shallowness_was_ruled_out_rather_tha: A shallow clone makes absence unsound, because a commit below the graft boundary is unreachable in the walk whether or not a ref contains it. This clone has one graft point. None of the ten named commits is an ancestor of it, so none can be concealed by the truncation -- tested per commit with merge-base --is-ancestor rather than argued from commit dates, which rebases make unreliable. A commit that could be concealed is now reported as indeterminate and fails the harness, rather than being reported as stranded.
how_the_zero_remote_refs_claim_was_actua.result: The fresh isolated audit names 12 distinct commits: 4 are contained by advertised origin refs, 6 are on no advertised ref but remain directly fetchable by SHA, and 2 are neither ref-contained nor directly fetchable at measurement time.

two_defects_in_the_first_version_of_that.an_allowlist_that_under_covered: I extracted provenance shas from three key names I expected, which found seven of the eleven object-shaped values the records carry and silently missed base_commit, built_on_main, candidate_commit and commit_on_main_carrying_this_source. It therefore reported zero resolvable commits, which should have been impossible given 15b0b11f0 is on main. The tell was that the answer was too clean. Any object-shaped value in provenance is now a candidate.
two_defects_in_the_first_version_of_that.object_type_was_assumed: producing_tree_identity holds a TREE, not a commit. Asking whether a tree is on a branch is a category error, not a finding. Type is checked with cat-file -t and non-commits are reported separately.
two_defects_in_the_first_version_of_that.orphaned_tracking_refs_counted_as_remote: This clone carries refs under refs/remotes/ belonging to remotes that no longer exist -- npabase627, npapr607 and 69 others -- which are as local as any branch. They inflated one commit's reachability to 684 refs. Reachability is now scoped to configured remotes, with orphans counted separately. The direction was safe for the stranded verdict, since a wider net can only find more, but 'another reader can resolve this' is a claim about the remote.

the_finding_broke_one_of_my_own_tests_in.what_happened: test_the_recovered_commits_are_the_ones_the_records_name traced each recovered commit with git log -S and asserted the named sha was found. It passed here and failed in CI from the first push, and I had reported the branch as red only on the queue-wide dependency gate, which was wrong.
the_finding_broke_one_of_my_own_tests_in.why_it_failed: The CI clone did not contain the unreferenced source objects, so git log -S over that clone could not reproduce the author's local trace.
the_finding_broke_one_of_my_own_tests_in.the_fix: The deterministic check now binds each record to its recovery-table probe and proves that probe exists under npa/ in the named main commit but not its parent. It cannot be self-satisfied by evidence prose or the test's own literals.
the_finding_broke_one_of_my_own_tests_in.what_i_should_have_noticed_sooner: I read the shard results as one red check and did not open them. The failure had been there since the first push and moved shards when I added tests, which is what finally made me look.

merge_refs_are_now_tested_rather_than_sk.what_the_first_version_did: Skipped refs/pull/*/merge, arguing a merge ref has its PR head as an ancestor and so cannot hold a commit the head lacks.
merge_refs_are_now_tested_rather_than_sk.what_a_reviewer_found: The property holds for every merge ref on this remote, but for one of them it holds for a different reason than the one I gave: the head had moved since the merge ref was last computed, so the merge ref was behind rather than derived from the current head. Harmless there. A force-push is the case that would not be harmless.
merge_refs_are_now_tested_rather_than_sk.the_fix: They are fetched and tested with everything else. An audit about commits hiding on forgotten refs should not rest on an argument about refs when the measurement costs one more refspec. Including them changed no verdict, which is the empirical version of the reviewer's analysis.
merge_refs_are_now_tested_rather_than_sk.a_count_i_published_that_was_stale_on_ar: I wrote 23 merge refs in prose. The harness measured 24, and the remote now advertises 25. This repository gains refs continuously, so a count written into prose is wrong almost immediately. Counts live in the report and the prose points there.
merge_refs_are_now_tested_rather_than_sk.i_deleted_the_argument_from_my_commit_me: The code fetched and iterated merge refs, and my commit message said the justification was gone. It was still in the module docstring, because I made the edit with a string replace whose anchor no longer matched after the file had been reformatted, and it failed silently. A reviewer found a confident reason to skip merge refs sitting above a code path that ignores it. Two hardcoded ref counts in the same docstring survived the same way, in the very change whose point was that these counts go stale. Fixed with an edit that fails loudly.

what_this_changes_enforcement_does_not_r.the_finding: A reviewer measured the whole evidence directory instead of the records this change rewrote, and found files that carry digests, declare no provenance, and are not capability-record-*, so nothing inside this glob will ever reach them.
what_this_changes_enforcement_does_not_r.my_independent_count: 6 files carry digests with no provenance block, 5 of them the same files the reviewer named. The differences are population and base: their measurement was on main, this branch is 310 commits behind it, and one of their seven does not yet exist here.
what_this_changes_enforcement_does_not_r.why_it_is_reported_and_not_fixed_here: Widening the glob means designing provenance for six artifacts this change did not produce, on a stale base where the set is incomplete. That is a different change with its own review surface. The audit now reports the count so the enforcement edge is visible rather than silent, which is the part that was actually wrong.

Named no commit. `git log -S` for the regression test it lists finds exactly one: 6e8cd115f, whose message restates this record's capability line and which predates the record's own recorded_at by four minutes.
two_commits_were_recovered_not_invented.capability-record-support-claim-correcti: Named no commit. `git log -S FAR_BAND_AREA_SHARE`, the rename it describes, finds exactly one: 16012b108, committed 45 seconds after the record's recorded_utc -- consistent with writing the record and then committing.
two_commits_were_recovered_not_invented.capability-record-view-framing.json: Named only the two files that produced it, which is a different fact. 256c26bc915 restates its capability line almost verbatim and was committed two seconds before its recorded_at.
two_commits_were_recovered_not_invented.why_this_is_not_guesswork: Each search returned exactly one commit, and in each case the commit message, the record's capability line and the timestamps agree independently. Where no such evidence existed I would have used a null with a reason rather than a best guess.

negative_controls_that_fire: A record with no `provenance` object: caught, which is the state ten of them were in.
A `source_commit` carrying prose beside the sha -- the real pre-fix state of capability-record.json: caught as unparseable.
A commit named without the ancestry flag: caught.
An ancestry flag that contradicts the repository: caught.
A commit this clone cannot resolve, claimed as an ancestor: caught, because a clone that has main has every ancestor of main, so absence refutes the claim.
A null `source_commit` with no stated reason: caught. Declining to name a commit is allowed; declining silently is not.

i_mutation_tested_the_guard.why: A review lane previously found a test of mine that passed when the thing it claimed to check was mutated, and mutation testing on the sibling branch found a second such hole yesterday. Asserting coverage is not evidence of it.
i_mutation_tested_the_guard.result: 8 of 8 mutations killed, after one survived and was fixed.
i_mutation_tested_the_guard.the_one_that_survived: Disabling the 'commit named without the ancestry flag' branch. The missing key falls through to the comparison and is reported as claiming an ancestry of 'absent' -- which no record claims. The guard still exits 1, so a test asserting the exit code or the key name cannot tell the two apart. I reproduced both messages side by side rather than reasoning about it, then tightened the test to assert which check fired.
i_mutation_tested_the_guard.why_that_mattered_beyond_the_test: The fallthrough message is wrong about what the author did. A guard that misreports the defect it found costs more time than one that stays quiet.

the_clone_this_was_validated_in_is_shall.what: This worktree's repository is a shallow clone, so the absence inference -- a clone holding main holds every ancestor of main -- does not hold here and the guard declines to draw it.
the_clone_this_was_validated_in_is_shall.found_how: A negative control failed. I had written it to drive the inference through the guard's subprocess, and it reported no finding. The guard was right and the test was wrong about its environment.
the_clone_this_was_validated_in_is_shall.consequence_for_the_tests: The two absence controls now call the function with the git helpers replaced, so they test the inference itself rather than whatever the host happened to fetch. A control that passes or vanishes depending on clone depth looks like coverage and is not.
the_clone_this_was_validated_in_is_shall.consequence_for_the_guard: The skipped case is printed loudly to stderr and named per record, because the summary counts would otherwise read as though those records' ancestry had been checked.

what_this_does_not_establish: Nothing about whether any record's measurements are right. A correctly flagged commit can still be the wrong commit.
No product behavior change: no file under npa/src/ is touched.
Not remote reachability. The offline guard reports only missing origin-tracking refs in its current clone and points to the isolated network audit for advertised-ref and direct-SHA evidence.
Nothing about the three records whose provenance was already in the target shape; two are edited by open PRs and are left alone.
a_mistake_i_made_doing_this: My first run wrote a 40-character sha for the 602 merge that I had produced by padding the abbreviation, rather than resolving it. The script's own assertion caught it on the first record. It is the exact failure this change is about -- a provenance value that looks authoritative and resolves to nothing -- and I made it while fixing it.

provenance.why_no_source_commit: The harness and the ten rewritten records are added by this change, so the record cannot name its own commit -- the hash does not exist until after the record is written. The guard accepts a null with a reason for exactly this case, and the file digest below is what a reader can recompute now.
provenance.why_this_shape: A review lane found provenance recorded six different ways across these records, so an auditor had to learn each file. This is the one shape. A record about provenance that carried none would have been the defect it complains about.
provenance.reachability_audit: docs/evidence/open3d/commit-reachability-audit.json, produced by harness/audit_commit_reachability.py. Re-running it requires network access to the remote, so it is evidence rather than a CI gate; the committed report is what the tests check.
provenance.one_of_these_pins_goes_stale_when_the_au: commit-reachability-audit.json is bound by hash and is also the harness's own output, so re-running the audit invalidates the pin until it is re-bound. That is the intended behaviour -- a stale pin is a visible failure, where an unbound report is a silent one -- but it means the audit is not a thing to re-run casually.
